# PROCESS — what I did this iteration (explainability; REQUIRED)

Fill this in as you work. It is the human-readable record of HOW this iteration was done and is snapshotted with the candidate, so anyone — and the next iteration via ./prior_iterations/ — can see your reasoning. Be concrete.

## Ranked issue list (clusters by # failing tasks × trials, biggest first)
| rank | cluster | tasks | shared root cause | tag (KNOWLEDGE / BEHAVIORAL / CAPABILITY-GAP) | planned change class |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Partial/underspecified passenger write | 40 | Agent submits only the changed passenger (and/or drops dob) to update_reservation_passengers → env rejects on count mismatch or writes an incomplete roster → DB reward 0 | CAPABILITY-GAP (arg the tool can repair) | in-body normalize-then-call wrapper (lever 1) |
| 2 | Net charge/refund not communicated | 11 (also latent in any flights/baggage change) | After a cabin downgrade the exact refund ($5244) is never stated to the user → COMMUNICATE reward 0 even when DB is right | KNOWLEDGE + return-shape | enriched return `payment_summary` (lever 8) + docstring |
| 3 | Cancel/modify eligibility misjudged | 19, 37 | Agent can't cheaply tell if a reservation is cancellable (24h / business / insurance) or whether basic_economy may change cabin → wrong act/refuse or stall | KNOWLEDGE | derived `_policy_facts` on read (lever 8) + docstrings |
| 4 | Booking arg friction | 8, 25, 23 | payment key alias / insurance enum drift raises opaque errors; core failures also involve wrong flight selection (not tool-repairable) | KNOWLEDGE + arg-normalize | input normalization + slot-filling docs (levers 1/7) |
| 5 | Wrong-flight / wrong-reservation / execution stalls | 8, 12, 17, 22, 23, 25 | Reader picks the wrong entity or narrates without executing; not deterministically repairable from wrapper args without task-specific values | BEHAVIORAL / CAPABILITY-GAP | deliberately NOT patched with an overfit guard (see skipped) |

## Changes made this iteration (one row per edit — aim for MULTIPLE classes, incl. a NEW tool when a cluster needs one)
| cluster | edit class | file / tool | what & why it generalizes | protects passing? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | code / normalize-then-call | update_reservation_passengers.py | Fetch current roster; if submitted list ≤ current count and each submitted passenger maps unambiguously (first+last, else unique first name), rebuild the FULL roster applying submitted fields as overrides and back-filling missing dob. Generalizes to ANY partial passenger edit. | Yes — only fires when list fits AND every entry matches; a correct full list, a first-name rename with no match, or an oversize list all pass through byte-for-byte. |
| 2 | code / enriched return + doc | update_reservation_flights.py | Diff payment_history pre/post, add `payment_summary` stating the exact net charge/refund + "tell the user this exact amount"; docstring clarifies basic_economy MAY change cabin on identical segments. | Yes — additive field only; write args unchanged, so DB result identical to baseline. |
| 2 | code / enriched return + doc | update_reservation_baggages.py | Same payment_history diff → `payment_summary`; docstring pins $50/bag and total-vs-nonfree meaning. | Yes — additive field only; args forwarded unchanged. |
| 3 | code / enriched return + doc | get_reservation_details.py | Add derived `_policy_facts` (booked_within_24h vs 2024-05-15 15:00, cabin, insurance, cancellation_possible, cancellation_note, modification_note). Read-only hints; agent still decides. | Yes — read tool, no writes; purely additive field. |
| 4 | code / input-normalize + doc | book_reservation.py | Map insurance to exact 'yes'/'no' enum; rewrite payment key aliases (payment_method_id/id/payment → payment_id); literal per-param slot-filling docs for the weak reader. | Yes — normalization only touches malformed inputs that would otherwise error; valid inputs unchanged. |
| 3 | code / enriched return + doc | cancel_reservation.py | Docstring eligibility gate (24h/business/insurance + covered-reason + already-flown→human); add `refund_summary` from payment_history diff. | Yes — additive field only; args forwarded unchanged. |

## Verify-the-fix (one line per change: the trace it targets → what the guard/computation/new-tool now does on those exact inputs)
- Task 40 (passengers): submitted `[{first_name:"Mei", last_name:"Garcia"}]` (1 of 2, no dob) → repaired to gold `[{Anya,Garcia,1992-11-12},{Mei,Garcia,1989-12-13}]`. Verified in /tmp/verify_pax.py: exact gold match; reversed-order and full-correct inputs also normalize to gold; first-name-rename-no-match and oversize inputs pass through unchanged (5/5 cases).
- Task 11 (flights): business→basic_economy round trip, 3 pax → env appends payment amount −5244 → `payment_summary` = "REFUNDED $5244 … tell the user this exact amount: $5244" (matches gold communicate substring 5244). Refund math independently confirmed: (561+1339−53−99)×3 = 5244.
- Tasks 19/37 (cancel/modify): get_reservation_details now returns cancellation_possible + notes so the reader can justify the act/refuse and knows basic_economy cabin changes are allowed; cancel docstring states the exact predicate.
- Task 8/25/23 (booking friction): insurance and payment-key normalization remove opaque arg errors on the booking path (does not fix the wrong-flight root cause, so these may not flip — normalization is safe/general regardless).

## Process & features used
- Subagents / worktrees / parallel features used (or: "serial fallback because …"): Serial — single-model diagnosis over all 10 trajectory files + tasks.json gold actions + evaluator/env source; edits are few and tightly coupled so parallel fan-out added no value.
- Prior iterations I read from ./prior_iterations/ + ./RUNMAP.md (which, and what I learned): None — this is iteration 1/1 (seed baseline only, RUNMAP/LEDGER empty). rejected.jsonl empty, so no refuted edits to avoid.

## Good things to PRESERVE (do not let a future iteration undo these)
- The passenger auto-repair's SAFETY envelope: it must fire ONLY when the submitted list fits the roster and every entry matches unambiguously; never expand an oversize list or a no-match rename. This is what keeps it from regressing a correct full-roster write.
- Enrichment fields are ADDITIVE and never alter forwarded write args — this is why DB reward cannot regress. Keep payment_summary/refund_summary/_policy_facts as read-only extras.

## Deliberately skipped (cluster + why — already-passing / needs gold / infra noise)
- Composite atomic-write tool for the stall cluster (17, 25, 23): would only help if the weak reader SELECTS it AND fills it correctly, which I cannot verify without running eval this iteration; higher regression risk on held-out. Left for a future iteration with a run signal.
- Wrong-flight (8) / wrong-reservation (22) / wrong-decision (12): the only deterministic "fix" would key on task-specific ids/flights (overfit, fails held-out gate). No general wrapper-side repair exists, so not patched.
- nonfree_baggages silent override: ordering/allowance-dependent and not reconstructable from wrapper args without risking a passing task — skipped.
